reviews.review: This is one of those classics. It's pretty difficult but once you get the hang of how the game works it isn't so bad. Lots of different items to collect and push forward with. Gets pretty repetitive after a while. If you've played Risk of Rain 2, I'd recommend trying this one to see where they got their inspiration from.

Playing this after playing risk of rain 2 is a very strange experiance.

Positive:

Gameplay 9/10: Blasting hoards of pixelated monsters is about as fun as it sounds (pretty damn fun)

Graphics 9/10: For a 2D pixel-art game, the graphics are really nice. It's not impossible to tell what the characters and enemies are supposed to look like. 

Soundtrack 10/10: As always, Chris Christodoulou nailed the music on this. Coalescence, precipitation, and tropic of cancer are my personal favorites.

Negative:

For a platformer game, the platforming can be very annoying. Especially on maps like ancient valley that have a lot of rope-to-rope jumps. It's not that big of an issue, but it can make some levels less fun

Multiplayer does not seem to work. Whenever I try searching for a multiplayer server, my game crashes. Not sure if this is just a me thing, but if it isn't, Hopoo- I mean- Gearbox should probably fix it soon.

Other notes:

In risk of rain 2, monsoon mode is the final challenge difficulty that is there to test the players skills. In this game, monsoon mode feels like the absurdly hard difficulty that was added in as a joke. Even rainstorm mode is challenging. either I have no skill, or there was a massive drop in difficulty from this game to it's sequel.

They should give providence more dialouge. I wasn't really sure what to make of his character from the 8 brief quotes he gets.

Commando is, as always, weak

Loader is, as always, overpowered.

They need to add Chef to ror2. The customers would be pleased.
____________________________________________________________________

Final score: 9.5 out of 10
I'm not the only one that saw the dancing golems... right?

Has Acrid? Yes
Has Chef? Yes
